title: Externally driven condensates show translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion in viscoelastic media
one_liner_zh: 该文通过理论建模研究外部驱动下凝聚体在黏弹性介质中的极化、定向聚并与反常扩散，虽对象为相分离凝聚体且涉及互作动力学，但无具体蛋白互作或AI/物理模拟方法，机制建模思路对IDR介导的PPI相分离有启发。
abstract: Phase separation into compositionally and physically distinct domains is ubiquitous in (non)living matter ranging from alloys and emulsions to biomolecular condensates in cells. The organization of these domains can be controlled, for example, by nonequilibrium chemical reactions, external fields, or mechanical stresses. In this context, stationary states can emerge from effective long-range interactions resembling the electrostatics of charges. As shown here, externally controlled dynamic states, such as condensate motion, lead to an effective polarization and dipolar force fields even for microscopically nonpolarizable matter. The dipole-dipole interactions resulting from this \emph{translation-induced polarization} cause directed coalescence of domains. This coarsening mechanism complements Ostwald ripening and coalescence due to Brownian motion or Marangoni flows, and has implications for controlling domains by electric fields or concentration gradients. Interestingly, the chemical potential gradients around a domain that nucleates material are exactly opposite to the hydrodynamic pressure gradients around an impermeable colloid that pushes the fluid, suggesting a competition between phase separation and hydrodynamics. In addition to chemical control, the motion of domains can also be driven by mechanical stresses. An example is the cell interior, where mechanical stresses are actively generated by molecular motors and opposed by passive viscoelastic stresses in the cytoplasm and nucleoplasm. The resulting fluid flows lead to Brownian motion with a suppressed or enhanced size scaling which modifies collision-coalescence. For active stresses with a long correlation time, the domains show superdiffusion on intermediate time scales. Together, these findings shed new light on the dynamics of domains in viscoelastic media and conserved order parameters in general.
abstract_zh: 相分离（phase separation）形成组成和物理性质不同的区域，在（非）生命物质中普遍存在，范围从合金、乳液到细胞中的生物分子凝聚体。这些区域的组织可通过非平衡化学反应、外部场或机械应力等方式加以控制。在此背景下，稳态可由类似于电荷静电学的有效长程相互作用产生。如本文所示，外部控制的动态状态（如凝聚体运动）即使对于微观上不可极化的物质，也会导致有效极化和偶极力场。由这种“平移诱导极化”（translation-induced polarization）产生的偶极-偶极相互作用引起区域的定向聚并。这种粗化机制补充了奥斯特瓦尔德熟化（Ostwald ripening）以及由布朗运动或马兰戈尼流（Marangoni flows）引起的聚并，并对通过电场或浓度梯度控制区域具有启示意义。有趣的是，围绕成核物质区域的化学势梯度与围绕不可渗透胶体（推动流体）的流体动力学压力梯度恰好相反，这表明相分离与流体动力学之间存在竞争。除化学控制外，区域的运动也可由机械应力驱动。一个例子是细胞内部，其中机械应力由分子马达主动产生，并由细胞质和核质中的被动黏弹性应力所抵抗。由此产生的流体流动导致布朗运动具有抑制或增强的尺寸标度，从而改变碰撞-聚并行为。对于具有长相关时间的主动应力，区域在中间时间尺度上表现出超扩散。综合来看，这些发现为黏弹性介质中区域的动力学以及一般守恒序参量提供了新的见解。
